diagnostics.message: module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_function.scale_up builds a vpc_config from var.lambda_subnet_ids/var.lambda_security_group_ids, but it only depends on aws_iam_role.scale_up. module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.scale_up_vpc_execution_role (which grants ec2:CreateNetworkInterface etc.) depends on the same role and subnet inputs and is therefore unordered relative to the function. Lambda rejects creation of a VPC-attached function whose execution role cannot create ENIs, so the function must be ordered after the attachment (add depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.scale_up_vpc_execution_role]).

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_function.scale_down has a vpc_config but no ordering against module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.scale_down_vpc_execution_role; both depend only on aws_iam_role.scale_down and the subnet/security-group inputs, so Terraform may create the VPC-attached function before its role can create ENIs (Lambda creation fails with "The provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface on EC2"). Add an explicit depends_on on the attachment.

module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook creates a vpc_config from var.lambda_subnet_ids/var.lambda_security_group_ids, but nothing orders it after module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role, which grants the ENI permissions the VPC-attached function needs at creation time. Both hang off aws_iam_role.webhook_lambda, so the ordering is undefined; add depends_on on the attachment.

module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_lambda_function.pool configures vpc_config from var.config.lambda.subnet_ids/security_group_ids, but it is only ordered against aws_iam_role.pool. module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.pool_vpc_execution_role depends on the same role/config inputs, so the function may be created before the role has VPC execution permissions, which Lambda rejects. Add depends_on on the attachment.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_lambda_function.syncer creates a vpc_config from var.lambda_subnet_ids/var.lambda_security_group_ids but is not ordered against module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.syncer_vpc_execution_role; both depend only on aws_iam_role.syncer_lambda and the subnet inputs. A VPC-attached function whose execution role lacks ENI permissions fails to create, so an explicit depends_on is required.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_s3_object.trigger exists only to fire the syncer Lambda on first deployment (S3 event on triggers/*.json). Its depends_on chain covers only the notification and the resource-based invoke permission, not the syncer's execution role policy: module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.syncer grants the s3:PutObject on the distribution bucket and is unordered relative to the uploaded object. IAM policy changes are eventually consistent, so the first invocation can fail with AccessDenied, leaving the distribution bucket empty and the runners' user data (s3://<bucket>/<key>) with no binary to install. Add depends_on on aws_iam_role_policy.syncer (and the syncer logging policy).
